source_text: λόγον, ἢ παρὰ τὰς γραφὰς δόξουσιν ποιεῖν. 5.9 τῇ γὰρ ἐν μιᾷ θεότητι τριάδι οὐ συντάττεταί τι, οὔτε τὰ πνεύματα διὰ τὸ κεκλῆσθαι πνεύματα, κἂν μὴ τὰ βέβηλα εἴποιμεν, οὔτε οἱ ἄνθρωποι διὰ τὸ κεκλῆσθαι θεοί· οὐ γάρ ἐσμεν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ. εἰ δὲ οὐκ οἰηθῶσιν ἀντιπίπτειν αὐτοῖς τό· «μόνῳ σοφῷ θεῷ», καί· «μόνος ἔχων ἀθανασίαν·» οὐ δυνήσονται ἀπ' οὐδενὸς ἐξ ἐναντίας τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος κατασοφίζεσθαι. ταῦτα γὰρ οὕτως ὑπὸ Παύλου ἐρρήθη, διὰ τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγον μὲν τὸν υἱόν, πνεῦμα δὲ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα τυγχάνειν, καὶ ἀχωρίστως αὐτοῦ ἔχειν κατὰ τὴν φύσιν, καὶ εἰς μίαν ἀνάγεσθαι θεότητα, ὡς καὶ παρὰ τοῖς ἔξω λέγεται· εἷς θεὸς αὐτοπάτωρ, ἐξ οὗ τάδε πάντα γένοντο. 5.10 ὡς τοίνυν περὶ τοῦ πατρὸς Παῦλος Ῥωμαίοις, Γαλάταις καὶ Τιμοθέῳ γέγραφεν· «εἷς ὁ θεὸς,» οὕτω περὶ μὲν τοῦ υἱοῦ Ἰωάννης εἶπεν· «ὁ μονογενὴς θεός, ὁ ὢν ἐν τοῖς κόλποις τοῦ πατρός.» περὶ δὲ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος Παῦλος Κορινθίοις ἐδίδαξεν· «ἄλλῳ δὲ χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων ἐν τῷ ἑνὶ πνεύματι·» τὸ γὰρ ἑνιαῖον τῆς θείας καὶ ἀπληθύντου φύσεως ἴδιον. καὶ καθὰ ἐγράφη, ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς ἐγεννήθη, καὶ μαρτυρῶν λέγει· «ἐγὼ παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐξῆλθον·» οὕτως ἐγράφη, καὶ ὁ αὐτὸς εἶπεν· «τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὃ παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκπορεύεται,» ἤγουν ἐξεπορεύθη. 5.11 καὶ ὥσπερ ὁ υἱὸς θεὸς καὶ κύριος ὥν, τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ κυρίου ἐστὶν υἱός· οὕτω τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, θεὸς καὶ κύριος ὥν, τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ κυρίου ἐστὶν πνεῦμα. καὶ ὃν τρόπον λόγος γέγραπται ὁ υἱὸς διὰ τὸ συνυπάρχειν τῷ πατρί, τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα γέγραπται «ῥῆμα τοῦ θεοῦ» καὶ «πνεῦμα τοῦ στόματος» αὐτοῦ καὶ «πνοὴ παντοκράτορος», ἐπειδὴ συνυφεστὼς ἐξέλαμψεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ· ἵνα μὴ ἔξωθεν αὐτὸ τῆς θεότητος τοῦ πατρὸς ἢ τοῦ λόγου αὐτοῦ εἶναί τις ὑπολάβῃ. ἴδιον γὰρ τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦ λόγου, καὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ νοῦ· καὶ πληροῦται τό· «ὁ εἷς θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ πάντων, καὶ ἐπὶ πάντων καὶ διὰ πάντων καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν.» 5.12 καὶ καθὰ ὁ υἱὸς δείκνυται ἀπαράλλακτος τοῦ πατρός, ᾖ γράφει· «ὁ ἑορακὼς ἐμὲ ἑόρακε τὸν πατέρα·» ὡσαύτως καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα δι' ὧν φάσκει· «ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν, ὅτι ἐν ἡμῖν ἐστιν ὁ θεός, ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ, οὗ ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν.» ἀνάγκη οὖν πᾶσα, θεοῦ ἀληθινοῦ ὄντος τοῦ πατρός, θεὸν ἀληθινὸν εἶναι ἴσον 52 αὐτῷ καὶ τὸν δεικνύντα αὐτὸν τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ἐμφανείᾳ. 5.13 καὶ ὥσπερ διὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ πάντα ἐγένετο, οὕτως ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος πάντα ἡγιάσθη καὶ ἐδυναμώθη. φασὶν γὰρ οἱ ἀπόστολοι· «δέσποτα, ὁ ποιήσας τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασ σαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς· ὁ διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου, στόματος δὲ ∆αυὶδ παιδός σου εἰκών.» καὶ καθὰ ἰσοδύναμος καὶ ὅμοιος ὁ μονογενὴς τῷ πατρὶ καὶ ἐξουσιαστὴς σημαίνεται κατὰ τό· «ὅσα ἂν ποιῇ ὁ πατήρ, ταῦτα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς ὁμοίως ποιεῖ» ὡσαύτως καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ τό· «πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἐνεργεῖ τὸ ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα.» 5.14 καὶ ὥσπερ περὶ ἑαυτοῦ εἶπεν ὁ Χριστός· «οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα, εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς,» οὕτω καὶ περὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος τὸ ὅμοιον εἴρηται, ὅτι· «τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐδεὶς ἔγνω, εἰ μὴ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ.» καὶ ὃν τρόπον ὁ υἱὸς τὸ ἀγγελτικόν, «μεγάλης βουλῆς ἄγγελος» ἐκλήθη· οὕτω καὶ περὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος· φησὶν γάρ· «ἀλλὰ ἐλάβομεν τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα εἰδῶμεν τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ χαρισθέντα ἡμῖν.» 5.15 καὶ ὁμοιότατον τῷ· «ἀπαρχὴ Χριστός,» τὸ λέγον ῥητόν· «καὶ τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τοῦ πνεύματος ἔχοντες.» καὶ ἰσοπαλὲς τῷ· «ὁ δὲ κύριος ἁγιάσαι ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἦτε εἰλικρινεῖς καὶ ἀπρόσκοποι εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπολυτρώσεως,» τό· «ἵνα γένηται ἡ προσφορὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν εὐπρόσδεκτος, ἡγιασμένη ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.» καὶ ἰσόρροπον τῷ εἰπεῖν· «ὁ ἀφορίσας με ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός μου, διὰ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἀποκαλύψαι ἐν ἐμοὶ τὸν Χριστὸν αὐτοῦ,» τό· «ἀπεκάλυψεν ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ.» 5.16 καὶ ἰσοδύναμον τῷ εἰπεῖν· «ἑαυτοὺς δοκιμάζετε, εἰ ὁ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν,» τὸ φάναι· «ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐ πνεῦμα τοῦ κόσμου ἐλάβομεν, ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ.» καὶ ἴσον τό· «οὐκ οἴδατε, ὅτι ναὸς θεοῦ ἐστε, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν;» τῷ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου γραφέντι· «ἐὰν ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους, ὁ θεὸς ἐν ὑμῖν μένει. ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ μένομεν καὶ αὐτὸς ἐν ἡμῖν ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ, οὗ ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν,» καὶ τῷ· «ἐλευσόμεθα ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ πατήρ, καὶ μονὴν παρ' αὐτῷ ποιήσομεν.» 5.17 καὶ ὥσπερ διὰ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα δίδοται κατὰ τό· «ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ πνεύματός μου ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα» καὶ κατὰ τό· «λάβετε πνεῦμα ἅγιον·» οὕτως διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ὁ Χριστὸς κατὰ τὸν Παῦλον Ἐφεσίοις γράφοντα· «ἵνα δῷ ὑμῖν,

pass_b_english: …the Word, or they will be seen to act against the Scriptures.

For nothing is ranked with the Trinity in one Godhead: not the spirits because they are called spirits, to say nothing of the profane ones; not human beings because they are called gods, for we are not gods in truth. And if they do not think that the words “to the only wise God” (Romans 16:27) and “who alone has immortality” (1 Timothy 6:16) tell against themselves, they will not be able to use anything at all to argue cleverly against the Holy Spirit. For Paul spoke in this way because the Son is the Word of God and the Holy Spirit is his Spirit, and they belong to him inseparably by nature and are referred back to one Godhead. Even among those outside it is said: “One God, self-fathered, from whom all these things came to be.”

As Paul, then, wrote of the Father to the Romans, the Galatians and Timothy, “God is one” (Romans 3:30; Galatians 3:20; 1 Timothy 2:5), so John said of the Son, “the only-begotten God, who is in the bosom of the Father” (John 1:18); and of the Holy Spirit Paul taught the Corinthians, “to another gifts of healing in the one Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:9). For oneness is proper to the divine nature, which is not multiplied. And as it was written that the Son was begotten, and he says in witness, “I came forth from the Father” (John 16:28), so it was written, and the same Lord said, “the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father” (John 15:26), that is, who proceeded.

And as the Son, being God and Lord, is the Son of God and Lord, so the Holy Spirit, being God and Lord, is the Spirit of God and Lord. And as the Son is written “Word” because he exists together with the Father, in the same way the Holy Spirit is written “utterance of God” (Ephesians 6:17), and “breath of his mouth” (Psalm 33:6), and “breath of the Almighty” (Job 33:4), since, subsisting together with him, he shone forth from him; so that no one may suppose him to be outside the Godhead of the Father or of his Word. For the utterance belongs to the word, and the word to the mind; and so the saying is fulfilled, “the one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all” (Ephesians 4:6).

And as the Son is shown to be indistinguishable from the Father where it is written, “He who has seen me has seen the Father” (John 14:9), so is the Holy Spirit, by the words, “By this we know that God is in us, by his Spirit whom he has given us” (1 John 3:24). It is altogether necessary, then, since the Father is true God, that he too who shows him by his own manifestation should be true God, equal to him.

And as all things came to be through the Son (John 1:3), so by the Spirit all things were sanctified and empowered. For the apostles say: “Master, you who made heaven and earth and the sea and all that is in them, who through the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of David your servant, [said]” (Acts 4:24–25). And as the Only-begotten is shown to be equal in power with the Father, like him, and sovereign, according to the words, “Whatever the Father does, these things the Son also does likewise” (John 5:19), so too is the Spirit of God, according to the words, “All these things the one and the same Spirit works” (1 Corinthians 12:11).

And as Christ said of himself, “No one has known the Father except the Son” (Matthew 11:27), so the like is said of the Holy Spirit: “No one has known the things of God except the Spirit of God” (1 Corinthians 2:11). And as the Son, because he announces, was called “Messenger of great counsel” (Isaiah 9:5 LXX), so it is with the Holy Spirit too, for Scripture says: “But we received the Spirit of God, that we might know the things freely given to us by God” (1 Corinthians 2:12).

Very like “Christ the firstfruits” (1 Corinthians 15:23) is the text that says, “and having the firstfruits of the Spirit” (Romans 8:23). Matched with “May the Lord sanctify you, that you may be pure and blameless for the day of redemption” is “that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable, sanctified in the Holy Spirit” (Romans 15:16). And of equal weight with saying, “He who set me apart from my mother’s womb, through his grace, to reveal his Christ in me” (Galatians 1:15–16), is “God revealed it through his Spirit” (1 Corinthians 2:10).

Of equal force with saying, “Examine yourselves, whether Christ is in you” (2 Corinthians 13:5), is the saying, “We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit of God” (1 Corinthians 2:12). And “Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you?” (1 Corinthians 3:16) is equal to what John wrote, “If we love one another, God abides in us. By this we know that we abide in him and he in us, by his Spirit whom he has given us” (1 John 4:12–13), and to “I and the Father will come and make our dwelling with him” (John 14:23).

And as the Holy Spirit is given through the Father and the Son, according to “I will pour out of my Spirit on all flesh” (Joel 2:28) and according to “Receive the Holy Spirit” (John 20:22), so through the Holy Spirit Christ is given, according to Paul, who writes to the Ephesians, “that he may grant you …

choices.issue: Edition numbers printed in the text, sentence broken off, garbled clauses, wrong references
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u13): retranslated from the Greek. The old English printed 5.13, 5.14, 5.15, 5.16 and 5.17 inside the reading text (the reader report on this section), cut 5.12 off at 'a true God be equal to him and—' and restarted a new paragraph mid-clause, rendered ἀπαράλλακτος 'distinct', τὸ ἑνιαῖον τῆς ἀπληθύντου φύσεως 'the plurality of nature', συνυφεστώς 'co-substanced', and garbled 5.9 ('the Trinity is not composed of something within the one divinity', 'made wise by anything from the opposite of the Holy Spirit') and 5.11 ('the word of the Word and the word of the mind are His own'). References fixed: (Acts 1:8) -> (John 20:22) for 'Receive the Holy Spirit'; (1 John 4:13) -> (1 John 3:24) in 5.12 and -> (1 John 4:12–13) in 5.16; (1 Cor 15:20) -> (1 Corinthians 15:23); (Gal 1:15) -> (Galatians 1:15–16); (Acts 4:24) -> (Acts 4:24–25); (Romans 3:30; 1 Cor 8:6) -> (Romans 3:30; Galatians 3:20; 1 Timothy 2:5); abbreviated names written out. Added: Romans 16:27, 1 Timothy 6:16, Ephesians 6:17, Psalm 33:6, John 1:3, 1 Corinthians 2:10, 2:11, 2:12 (twice), Romans 8:23, Romans 15:16, Isaiah 9:5 LXX. '[called]' brackets removed.

choices.term: λόγον, ἢ παρὰ τὰς γραφὰς δόξουσιν ποιεῖν
choices.english: …the Word, or they will be seen to act against the Scriptures.
choices.why: The sentence begins in the previous section ('they will either defraud God …'); only the words this section holds are translated, opened with '…'.

choices.english: to say nothing of the profane ones
choices.why: The unclean spirits are not even in question; Didymus sets them aside.

choices.term: εἰ δὲ οὐκ οἰηθῶσιν ἀντιπίπτειν αὐτοῖς
choices.english: if they do not think that the words … tell against themselves
choices.why: The heretics admit the Son is wise and immortal, so they do not take 'the only wise God' to exclude him; by the same rule the texts cannot be turned against the Spirit.

choices.term: εἷς θεὸς αὐτοπάτωρ, ἐξ οὗ τάδε πάντα γένοντο
choices.english: “One God, self-fathered, from whom all these things came to be.”
choices.why: A hexameter verse from pagan religious poetry ('those outside'); left without a reference.
Didymus distinguishes ῥῆμα (the Spirit) from λόγος (the Son); 'utterance' keeps the two apart. In 5.29 (u13-rem-close) he quotes Ephesians 6:17 for this title.
Psalm 32:6 in the Greek numbering, 33:6 in English; Didymus quotes the verse in full in 5.30.
Job 33:4 has the phrase word for word (also Job 32:8 in a longer form).

choices.term: «ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν, ὅτι ἐν ἡμῖν ἐστιν ὁ θεός ...»
choices.why: Didymus' wording ('that he is in us, by the Spirit he gave us') matches 1 John 3:24; 1 John 4:13 (the old reference) has 'that we abide in him and he in us', which Didymus quotes separately in 5.16.
52 is a printed page number in the copy-text, skipped.
A word split by a line break in the copy-text; read as θάλασσαν.
The copy-text has εἰκών, 'image', where Acts 4:25 reads εἰπών, 'who said'; one letter differs and 'image' makes no sense in the sentence. Bracketed as an editorial correction; see problems.

The Greek Bible's form of the verse: Rahlfs Isaiah 9:5 (English 9:6), where the Hebrew text behind the KJV reads 'Wonderful, Counsellor'; cited in Greek numbering with the LXX label because the wording is the Greek Bible's alone. 'Messenger' keeps the play on τὸ ἀγγελτικόν, his office of announcing.
Accusative of respect: the Son is called 'messenger' with respect to his office of making known the Father's will.
The exact two words are in 15:23; 15:20 (the old reference) has 'firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep'.

choices.term: «ὁ δὲ κύριος ἁγιάσαι ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἦτε εἰλικρινεῖς ...»
choices.why: A conflation of 1 Thessalonians 5:23, Philippians 1:10 and Ephesians 4:30; listed as possible allusions.

choices.english: to reveal his Christ in me
choices.why: Didymus' text reads 'his Christ' where Galatians 1:16 has 'his Son'; his wording is kept.
The copy-text has ὑμῖν, 'you', a common vowel confusion for ἡμῖν; 1 John 4:12 and the first person 'if we love' require 'us'.

choices.term: οὕτως διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ὁ Χριστός
choices.english: so through the Holy Spirit Christ is given
choices.why: The verb δίδοται carries over from the first half of the comparison; English needs it written.
The quotation (Ephesians 3:16–17) runs into the next section; only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'. The reference is placed where the quotation ends, in u13-rem-mid.
